ai_analysis.insight_zh: 谷歌通过发布gBench试图确立开源模型评测的话语权，通过内置大量代理任务测试，引导市场关注焦点从单纯的参数规模转向模型在复杂代理行为上的鲁棒性。此举将有助于加速闭源与开源模型在垂直领域性能对比的透明化。
ai_analysis.insight_en: By releasing gBench, Google seeks to establish influence over open-source model evaluation standards. By incorporating extensive agentic task tests, they are steering market focus away from parameter counts toward the robustness of models in complex agentic behavior, thereby accelerating transparency in performance benchmarking between open and closed models.

He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about
viral_ticker_tweets.title_zh:
他是对的。 我们正在经历思想的死亡。

刚才，我不得不阅读一篇由 AI 生成的 900 字的厚篇文章，内容是关于一个使用自动铅笔打印合同的人。

我没有浏览 12 秒，低声说“对他有好处”，然后继续我的夜晚，而是做了一些激进的事情。

我
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
He's right.  We are experiencing the death of thought.

Just now, I had to read a hefty AI-generated 900-word post about a guy who printed a contract and used a mechanical pencil.

Rather than skim it for 12 seconds, whisper “good for him,” and move on with my evening, I did something radical.

I didn’t print your post on a Wi-Fi laser printer like some kind of Silicon Valley soft-hands.

I transcribed every single one of your 902 words by hand onto unbleached calfskin vellum using a goose quill I cured in my own garage, sharpened it with a dull pocketknife until my thumb bled, and spent four and a half hours marking up the margins in homemade iron-gall ink.

I finished writing down my thoughts in the margins, set down my quill, stared silently at a brass lamp, and reflected on what just happened.

I felt deeply satisfied, wildly embarrassed, mildly dehydrated, and somehow taller all at once.

I couldn’t remember the last time I had used my brain for an end-to-end process without relying on an industrial convenience like a mechanical pencil or Hewlett-Packard toner. I felt total command over your post. I felt crystalline clarity about what I understood, what I didn’t understand, and why a grown man felt moved to alert the entire timeline that he had read a PDF with a pencil. And I was left with unshakable conviction in my POV.

Moreover, I felt the high of “ultra-clean” dopamine.

Not the factory-farmed, seed-oil dopamine you get from pressing a plastic thumb-clicker on a 0.7mm Pentel like a lab rat tapping a lever for pellets. Not the lukewarm, ultra-processed dopamine of reading a contract printed out on bleached 20-pound copy paper that a machine collated for you without even asking you to set the movable type.

No. I’m talking about single-origin, cold-pressed, pasture-raised dopamine. The kind of raw, unadulterated neurochemical high our ancestors felt when they sat down at a mahogany desk, read an actual contract from page one to the signature block, and didn’t immediately open LinkedIn to announce that they had survived the ordeal.

Then I felt embarrassed.

How long had I been depriving myself of turning basic adult errands into sweeping civilizational manifestos?

Just yesterday, I made two slices of sourdough toast without once asking Claude to “review this loaf, break down the crumb structure, and give me feedback as if you’re my baker.” I stood there in front of the toaster like a pioneer on the Oregon Trail, watched the heating coils glow orange, buttered the bread manually, and ate it. And what did I do afterward? Nothing. I just rinsed my plate and went to work. Not a single 1,000-word reflection on the erosion of culinary agency. Not one mention of Socrates. Not one bulleted list of ways to reclaim the sacred space between bread and butter.

I was disgusted with myself.

And then I got curious.

In fact, I got so curious that I had to sit down, because curiosity at this altitude can make a man lightheaded.

Why is it that every time somebody in tech rediscovers an office supply from 1987, he feels spiritually compelled to summon Daniel Kahneman, Socrates, and Viktor Frankl like the Avengers? And what can we do to make sure we don’t surrender our last remaining shred of self-awareness to the Thought Leadership Industrial Complex?

The answer lies in what Daniel Kahneman called System 1 and System 2 thinking, and more importantly, in the three higher systems that Kahneman was too polite to put in the book.

Everyone on the internet loves citing System 1 and System 2, mostly because Thinking, Fast and Slow is the single most-referenced book among people who read a four-page summary of it in 2016 and have been dining out on the phrase “lazy controller” ever since.

System 1 is fast, automatic, and gut-driven thought. It’s what fires when a 42-page commercial agreement lands in your inbox on a Thursday afternoon and your brain immediately says, “I am not reading all of this, I should probably pay an actual lawyer instead of asking a chatbot to roleplay as one.”

System 2 is deliberate, analytical, effortful, and conscious. It’s what fires when you ignore System 1, print the 42-page agreement yourself, grab a mechanical pencil, write “check indemnity??” and “what does mutatis mutandis mean” in the margins for 90 minutes, and walk away from your desk feeling like John Marshall presiding over Marbury v. Madison.

But stopping at System 2 is rookie-level cognition. If you really want to diagnose what is happening to the human mind in 2026, you have to go deeper:

System 3 is performing System 2 in public so strangers know you still have a prefrontal cortex. You didn’t merely read the contract. You observed yourself reading the contract from a cinematic third-person camera angle, felt a single noble tear roll down your cheek, and started mentally workshopping the opening hook somewhere around Section 7.2(b).

System 4 is taking a completely normal Tuesday afternoon task (reading a document before you sign it) and laundering it through one ancient Greek philosopher, three cognitive psychologists, a misattributed quote, ten repetitive bullet points, and a closing comparison to the sun until a routine administrative chore sounds like the drafting of the Magna Carta.

System 5 is reading someone else’s System 4 post and concluding that the only proportionate moral response is to construct an even longer, even more grandiose System 4 post, thereby testing the structural load limits of the X Premium character counter and everybody’s patience simultaneously.

Technology has been hijacking effortful thinking for far longer than 370 BC. Frankly, starting the timeline with Socrates is System 1 history.

Roughly a million years ago: Fire hijacked raw-meat mastication as a gastrointestinal System 2 exercise. Early hominids no longer had to chew elk cartilage for four uninterrupted hours just to extract 300 calories. Immediate metabolic offloading. Everything went downhill from there.

3200 BC: Sumerian cuneiform hijacked remembering how many goats your brother-in-law owed you from the spring harvest. Within two generations, nobody could keep track of a single goat in their head. Pure cognitive atrophy.

1440 AD: Gutenberg’s printing press hijacked the deeply satisfying, hard-fought labor of being a medieval monk squinting in an unheated stone scriptorium for eleven years to hand-copy one manuscript by tallow candle. Did anyone pause to ask what the printing press was doing to the monks’ taste?

1784: Bifocals hijacked squinting as an ocular System 2 exercise.

1822: John Isaac Hawkins and Sampson Mordan secured British Patent No. 4742 for the first mechanical pencil, explicitly designed in the words of the patent itself for “rendering the frequent cutting or mending of the points or nibs unnecessary.”

Stop and sit with that for a moment.

The very mechanical pencil you held aloft yesterday as your Excalibur against Silicon Valley is itself a 204-year-old machine engineered to offload the noble, character-building friction of whittling cedarwood with a blade and blowing graphite dust off your thumb. You didn’t reject shortcuts. You just picked a Victorian shortcut and called it enlightenment.

1959: The Xerox 914 photocopier hijacked retyping contracts on carbon paper.

1983: Microsoft Word hijacked Wite-Out and the healthy, adrenaline-soaked terror of making a typo on page 14 of a 15-page lease.

Calculators hijacked long division.
GPS hijacked arguing with your spouse over a folded Rand McNally road atlas on the center console while missing the exit for Savannah.
Google hijacked sitting at a bar for three hours insisting to your friends that Kevin Costner was in Air Force One when it was actually Harrison Ford, the kind of hard-fought, unadulterated barstool conviction that used to build real character.

Now, to be completely fair to you, you’re right about one big thing. AI really is different.

It doesn’t just take over one effortful job at a time. It takes over all of them at once.

Remembering. Summarizing. Researching. Calculating. Writing. Problem-solving. Weighing trade-offs. Deciding. Planning. Navigating people. Reflecting. Creating. Sounding like a 2019 Medium post. Putting “&” instead of “and” ten times inside a 5,300-character essay where nobody was running out of space. Using the verb “grok” unironically in a manifesto about resisting the machines. Building a ten-item bulleted list where four of the bullets are literally the same bullet wearing different sweaters.

For 200,000 years, our brains have been wired to take the easy out. And when we surrender to shortcuts, whether it’s letting an LLM read our contracts or letting LinkedIn formatting do the heavy lifting of sounding profound, we pay a steep price.

Let’s break down the real costs.

Cost 1: A summary feels like understanding, and a numbered framework feels like wisdom.

You’re completely right that reading a compressed summary tricks your brain into believing you understand a subject you never actually wrestled with. What gets overlooked is the mirror-image trap: taking a twelve-word piece of common sense (“If you don’t read the contract, you won’t know what’s in it”) and inflating it into a 900-word lecture about Paleolithic brain evolution tricks both the author and the reader into thinking they just witnessed a breakthrough in epistemology. Packaging isn’t insight. Single-line paragraphs aren’t depth.

Like this.

And this.

Notice how your brain wants to nod slowly right now, even though I haven’t said anything since the previous paragraph. That’s System 1 getting played by line breaks.

Cost 2: The messy middle is the space for growth, which is also where you discover that reviewing a hefty contract without a lawyer is an exciting way to buy a lawsuit.

Robert Bjork’s work on “desirable difficulties” at UCLA is genuinely great research, and Risko and Gilbert’s work on cognitive offloading is real too. Effortful retrieval makes learning stick. Nobody serious disagrees with that. The funny part is acting like desirable difficulty is an endangered species we have to artificially manufacture with “no-AI blocks,” as if real life isn’t already handing out nine hours of involuntary desirable difficulty every single weekday. Try closing a deal with a stubborn lender, managing a payroll when receivables slip, or reading Section 14.3(c) of a commercial lease where the other side quietly buried a personal guaranty inside a boilerplate maintenance clause. You don’t need a 10-minute productivity hack to experience cognitive friction. Just have actual skin in the game.

Cost 3: The disappearance of judgement, and the rise of the performative sigh.

You asked what will stay uniquely human as we approach AGI and ASI, and you gave us four pillars:

1. Intent
2. Accountability
3. Relationships
4. Judgement

Solid start. Respectable list. A little short, though. If we’re being honest about the final frontier of human uniqueness in the age of superintelligence, there are at least six more traits no neural network will ever truly replicate:

5. Printing a 30-page PDF so you can carry it around the house looking burdened and important.
6. Telling everybody at dinner that you’ve “been going really analog lately.”
7. Buying a $65 brass mechanical pencil from a specialty stationery shop in Kyoto so your margin notes have better mouthfeel.
8. Calling regular job satisfaction “clean dopamine” because saying “I felt good about finishing my work” doesn’t sound like a Huberman episode.
9. Assuming that because you used to outsource your thinking to Claude, the rest of Western civilization forgot how to read a document.
10. Confusing “having taste” with “posting about how important taste is.”

Taste really is thousands of compressed System 2 patterns firing at once. You know what one of those patterns looks like? Reading your own draft back before hitting Post and thinking, “Wait, did I really just compare myself reading a contract with a pencil to fighting for the survival of human thought?”

Cost 4: The Viktor Frankl Industrial Complex.

Every serious productivity essay on the internet must, by federal statute, include the exact quote:

“Between stimulus and response there is a space. In that space is our power to choose our response. In our response lies our growth and our freedom.”

It’s a lovely sentiment. There is just one tiny, delicious wrinkle.

Viktor Frankl never wrote it.

Researchers have searched Man’s Search for Meaning and the rest of Frankl’s published works top to bottom. Those words aren’t there. Stephen Covey popularized the line after coming across a similar passage in a university library book in Hawaii (scholars point to psychologist Rollo May’s 1963 writing on pausing between stimulus and response as the closest precursor), and somewhere around the mid-2000s the internet glued Viktor Frankl’s name onto it and never looked back.

Think about the sheer poetry of that. A few lines above your own bullet point commanding humanity to “Read the full source, not the summary,” you dropped the single most famous misattributed summary-culture quote on the entire internet.

If that isn’t a case study in cognitive offloading, nothing is.

Cost 5: The hyperinflation of metaphors.

Once upon a time, a contract was a contract and the sun was a 4.6-billion-year-old ball of fusing hydrogen plasma 93 million miles from Earth that grows crops, powers the water cycle, and gives you a leathery neck if you skip sunscreen on the back nine.

Now a probabilistic text engine that tells you “That’s a really sharp, nuanced point!” every time you misspell a question is “like the sun.”

If AI is the sun, what does that make the mechanical pencil? A patio umbrella? SPF 50? A pair of polarized sunglasses? Once you start comparing software subscriptions to nuclear fusion in space, you leave yourself nowhere to go when something actually important happens.

Cost 6: The collapse of proportionality.

When every minor personal realization (today I read a document carefully instead of skimming an AI bullet list!) has to be framed as an existential battle at the edge of the species, our collective sense of scale breaks down. Sometimes you didn’t strike a blow against the death of thought. Sometimes you just did your homework.

So how do we take back our thinking, our brevity, and our dignity, while still embracing this transformative technology?

It resolves down to one key principle: rebuild the space between having a normal afternoon and writing a 900-word sermon about it.

How you rebuild that space is completely up to you. Pick your poison:

- Create 30-to-60-minute no-AI blocks in your day, followed immediately by 90-minute no-posting blocks so you don’t undo the entire spiritual benefit by bragging about it online.
- Go analog and print out what matters. Then print out something that doesn’t matter at all, just to maintain dominance over your printer.
- Ditch the mechanical pencil. Use a wooden No. 2 and sharpen it with a pocketknife over a metal wastebasket like your grandfather did during the Eisenhower administration.
- Read the full source, not the summary, starting with Man’s Search for Meaning so you can see for yourself which quotes are actually inside it.
- When reviewing a hefty contract, instead of prompting Claude to act “as if you’re my lawyer,” try the radical, ancient analog workflow of hiring an actual lawyer.
- Write your first draft by hand. Write your second draft in wet sand at low tide so you learn non-attachment.
- Set a 10-minute rule: struggle with a problem for 10 minutes before reaching for AI. Then set a 20-minute rule: struggle with the urge to cite Daniel Kahneman before opening X.
- Say it out loud: explain your latest productivity realization to a bartender who cannot legally walk away from his register until you close your tab, and watch his eyes to gauge whether it’s actually profound.
- Memorize a paper highway map and refuse GPS even when you are 18 minutes late to dinner and your wife is staring silently out the passenger window. That icy silence in the front seat? That’s System 2 rebuilding itself in real time.
- Do your own long division on the back of a cocktail napkin at lunch so the table knows you still have skin in the cognitive game.
- Before hitting Post on any essay longer than 500 words, carve it into a slab of limestone with a chisel to test whether humanity truly needed it.
- Replace “grok” with “understand,” replace “&” with “and,” and replace “clean dopamine” with “I felt good about getting my work done.”
- Stare out a window for 15 unbroken minutes with zero inputs, zero podcasts, and zero mental models until you remember that “controlling the space between stimulus and response” used to just be called sitting quietly.
- Never summarize anything again. If a friend asks how a movie was, stand up and recite the entire screenplay from memory with full blocking and lighting cues.
- Treat AI as an “editor,” not a “writer.” That way, when it rewrites every single sentence for you anyway, you can still sleep soundly under the warm blanket of semantics.
- Ask yourself one final question before publishing anything about the future of human cognition: Would Socrates have typed this, or would he have asked for the hemlock twenty minutes early?

AI is like the sun.

Actually, if we’re applying a little System 2 rigor here, AI is nothing like the sun. The sun is a G-type main-sequence star holding eight planets in orbit through gravity that will eventually swell into a red giant and vaporize the earth. AI is a very fast autocomplete machine wired into a warehouse of GPUs that helps people turn a three-sentence email into a keynote about human destiny.

Yes, it may help cure cancer.
Yes, it may put a tutor in every child’s hands.
Yes, it may usher in an age of abundance, starting, apparently, with an unlimited abundance of 900-word essays by executives who just discovered paper and graphite.

It is powerful beyond measure. Which is why we must protect the final frontier of being human at all costs: knowing when to read the contract, put the pencil down, close the laptop, and not write a single word about it on the internet.

Anyway, I’ll be completely honest with you: I didn’t write a single word of this.

I pasted your post into my AI and told it to draft an extremely lengthy quote tweet at least twice as long as yours, because I had better things to do tonight and frankly it seemed funnier than thinking.

We must fight against the death of thought.
viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_zh:
他是对的。 我们正在经历思想的死亡。

刚才，我不得不阅读一篇由 AI 生成的 900 字的厚篇文章，内容是关于一个使用自动铅笔打印合同的人。

我没有浏览 12 秒，低声说“对他有好处”，然后继续我的夜晚，而是做了一些激进的事情。

我没有像硅谷的软手那样使用 Wi-Fi 激光打印机打印你的文章。

我用在自家车库里腌制的鹅毛笔，将你的 902 个单词中的每一个字都手写在未漂白的小牛皮牛皮纸上，用钝的小刀将其削尖，直到我的拇指流血，并花了四个半小时用自制的铁胆墨水标记边缘。

我在页边写完自己的想法，放下羽毛笔，默默地盯着一盏铜灯，思考着刚刚发生的事情。

我感到深深的满足、极度的尴尬、轻微的脱水，但不知何故突然长高了。

我不记得上次我在不依赖自动铅笔或惠普碳粉等工业便利设施的情况下使用大脑进行端到端流程是什么时候了。我对你的帖子感到完全掌控。我对自己理解的内容、不理解的内容感到非常清晰，也明白了为什么一个成年人会因为提醒整个时间线他用铅笔阅读了一份 PDF 而感到感动。我对自己的观点有着不可动摇的信念。

此外，我还感受到了“超洁净”多巴胺的快感。

不是工厂化养殖的种子油多巴胺，是通过在 0.7 毫米 Pentel 上按下塑料拇指点击器而获得的，就像实验室老鼠敲击颗粒杠杆一样。阅读打印在漂白的 20 磅复印纸上的合同时，机器会帮你校对，甚至不需要你设置活字印刷，这不是那种不冷不热、经过过度处理的多巴胺。

不，我说的是单一来源、冷榨、牧场饲养的多巴胺。当我们的祖先坐在桃花心木办公桌前，从第一页读到签名栏，阅读一份真实的合同，并且没有立即打开 LinkedIn 宣布他们已经从这场磨难中幸存下来时，他们感受到了那种原始的、纯粹的神经化学物质的兴奋。

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。
viral_ticker_tweets.author: Coastal Country Club
viral_ticker_tweets.summary_zh:
没有像硅谷的软手那样使用 Wi-Fi 激光打印机打印你的文章。

我用在自家车库里腌制的鹅毛笔，将你的 902 个单词中的每一个字都手写在未漂白的小牛皮牛皮纸上，用钝的小刀将其削尖，直到我的拇指流血，并花了四个半小时用自制的铁胆墨水标记边缘。

我在页边写完自己的想法，放下羽毛笔，默默地盯着一盏铜灯，思考着刚刚发生的事情。

我感到深深的满足、极度的尴尬、轻微的脱水，但不知何故突然长高了。

我不记得上次我在不依赖自动铅笔或惠普碳粉等工业便利设施的情况下使用大脑进行端到端流程是什么时候了。我对你的帖子感到完全掌控。我对自己理解的内容、不理解的内容感到非常清晰，也明白了为什么一个成年人会因为提醒整个时间线他用铅笔阅读了一份 PDF 而感到感动。我对自己的观点有着不可动摇的信念。

此外，我还感受到了“超洁净”多巴胺的快感。

不是工厂化养殖的种子油多巴胺，是通过在 0.7 毫米 Pentel 上按下塑料拇指点击器而获得的，就像实验室老鼠敲击颗粒杠杆一样。阅读打印在漂白的 20 磅复印纸上的合同时，机器会帮你校对，甚至不需要你设置活字印刷，这不是那种不冷不热、经过过度处理的多巴胺。

不，我说的是单一来源、冷榨、牧场饲养的多巴胺。当我们的祖先坐在桃花心木办公桌前，从第一页读到签名栏，阅读一份真实的合同，并且没有立即打开 LinkedIn 宣布他们已经从这场磨难中幸存下来时，他们感受到了那种原始的、纯粹的神经化学物质的兴奋。

然后我就觉得很尴尬。

我已经多久没有把基本的成人事务变成全面的文明宣言了？

就在昨天，我做了两片酵母吐司，一次都没有要求克劳德“检查这条面包，分解面包屑结构，并给我反馈，就像你是我的面包师一样。”我像俄勒冈小道上的拓荒者一样站在烤面包机前，看着加热线圈发出橙色的光，手动在面包上涂黄油，然后吃掉它。然后我做了什么？没有什么。我刚洗完盘子就去上班了。没有一篇关于烹饪机构受到侵蚀的千字反思。没有提到苏格拉底。没有一份详细的清单列出了重新夺回面包和黄油之间神圣空间的方法。

我对自己感到厌恶。

然后我很好奇。

事实上，我实在是太好奇了，不得不坐下来，因为在这种高度的好奇心会让人头晕目眩。

为什么每次科技领域的人重新发现 1987 年的办公用品时，他都会在精神上感到有必要像复仇者联盟一样召唤丹尼尔·卡尼曼、苏格拉底和维克托·弗兰克尔？我们能做些什么来确保我们不会将最后的一点自我意识拱手让给思想领导工业综合体？

答案就在于丹尼尔·卡尼曼所说的“系统1”和“系统2”的思维，更重要的是，在于卡尼曼出于礼貌而没有将其放入书中的三个更高的系统。

互联网上的每个人都喜欢引用系统 1 和系统 2，主要是因为《思考，快与慢》是人们在 2016 年读过该书长达四页的摘要并从那时起就一直在谈论“懒惰控制器”这个词的人中引用最多的一本书。

系统 1 是快速、自动、直觉驱动的思维。当周四下午一份 42 页的商业协议到达你的收件箱时，你的大脑立即说：“我不会阅读所有这些内容，我可能应该付钱给一名真正的律师，而不是让聊天机器人扮演律师。”

系统2是深思熟虑的、分析性的、努力的、有意识的。当你忽略系统 1，自己打印 42 页的协议，拿起自动铅笔，写下“检查赔偿？”时，就会触发这种情况。并在页边空白处写上“比照意味着什么”90 分钟，然后离开办公桌，感觉就像约翰·马歇尔在主持马伯里诉麦迪逊案。

但止步于系统2是菜鸟级别的认知。如果你真的想诊断 2026 年人类思维会发生什么，你必须更深入：

系统 3 在公共场合执行系统 ​​2，因此陌生人知道您仍然有前额皮质。您不仅仅阅读了合同。你观察到自己从电影般的第三人称视角阅读合同，感觉到一滴高贵的泪水从你的脸颊滚落，并开始在脑海中思考第 7.2(b) 节周围的开头钩子。

系统 4 正在执行一项完全正常的周二下午任务（在签署之前阅读一份文件），并通过一位古希腊哲学家、三位认知心理学家、一段错误引用、十个重复的要点以及与太阳的最终比较来对其进行清洗，直到日常行政琐事听起来像是起草《大宪章》。

系统 5 正在阅读其他人的系统 4 帖子，并得出结论，唯一相称的道德反应是构建一个更长、更宏伟的系统 4 帖子，从而同时测试 X Premium 角色计数器的结构负载限制和每个人的耐心。

自公元前 370 年以来，技术一直在劫持努力的思维。坦率地说，从苏格拉底开始的时间线就是系统 1 的历史。

大约一百万年前：火劫持了生肉咀嚼作为胃肠道系统 2 的锻炼。早期原始人类不再需要连续四个小时不间断地咀嚼麋鹿软骨来获取 300 卡路里的热量。立即代谢卸载。从那里开始一切都走下坡路。

公元前 3200 年：苏美尔楔形文字劫持了你的姐夫欠你多少春收的山羊。在两代人的时间里，没有人能够在头脑中记住一只山羊。纯粹的认知萎缩。

公元 1440 年：古腾堡的印刷机劫持了一位中世纪僧侣在没有暖气的石质写字间眯着眼睛用牛油蜡烛手抄一份手稿长达 11 年的令人深感满足的艰苦劳动。有没有人停下来问一下印刷机对僧侣们的口味做了什么？

1784 年：双焦点眼镜劫持了眯眼作为一种视觉系统 2 的锻炼方式。

1822 年：约翰·艾萨克·霍金斯 (John Isaac Hawkins) 和桑普森·莫丹 (Sampson Mordan) 为第一支自动铅笔获得了第 4742 号英国专利，专利本身的明确设计目的是“无需频繁切割或修补笔尖或笔尖”。

停下来坐一会儿。

昨天你在与硅谷对抗时高举的 Excalibur 机械铅笔本身就是一台拥有 204 年历史的机器，其设计目的是为了减轻用刀片削雪松木和吹掉拇指上的石墨粉尘时产生的高贵、塑造性格的摩擦。你没有拒绝捷径。你刚刚选择了一条维多利亚时代的捷径，并称之为启蒙。

1959 年：施乐 914 复印机劫持了在复写纸上重新打印合同的行为。

1983 年：Microsoft Word 劫持了 Wite-Out，以及在 15 页租约的第 14 页上犯错的健康、令人肾上腺素飙升的恐惧。

计算器劫持了长除法。
GPS 被劫持，您与配偶就中控台上折叠的兰德·麦克纳利道路地图集争论，同时错过了萨凡纳的出口。
谷歌劫持了在酒吧坐了三个小时，向你的朋友坚称凯文·科斯特纳在空军一号，而实际上是哈里森·福特，这种经过艰苦斗争、纯粹的酒吧凳信念用来塑造真实的性格。

现在，公平地说，你对一件大事的看法是正确的。人工智能确实不同。

它不仅仅一次接管一项艰苦的工作。它立刻接管了所有的人。

记住。总结一下。研究中。计算。写作。解决问题。权衡利弊。决定。规划。为人们导航。反思。创造。听起来像是 2019 年的 Medium 帖子。在一篇 5,300 字的文章中十次用“&”代替“and”，没有人会出现空间不足的情况。在关于抵抗机器的宣言中讽刺地使用了动词“grok”。建立一个包含十项项目符号的列表，其中四个项目符号实际上是相同的项目符号，穿着不同的毛衣。

20万年来，我们的大脑一直习惯于轻松出行。当我们屈服于捷径时，无论是让法学硕士阅读我们的合同，还是让LinkedIn格式完成听起来深刻的繁重工作，我们都会付出高昂的代价。

让我们来分解一下实际成本。

成本1：总结感觉像是理解，编号框架感觉像是智慧。

你完全正确，阅读压缩摘要会欺骗你的大脑，让你相信你理解了一个你从未真正思考过的主题。被忽视的是镜像陷阱：将一段 12 个字的常识（“如果你不读合同，你不会知道里面有什么”）并将其夸大为关于旧石器时代大脑进化的 900 字讲座，欺骗作者和读者，让他们认为他们刚刚见证了认识论的突破。包装不是洞察力。单行段落没有深度。

像这样。

还有这个。

注意你的大脑现在想要慢慢点头，尽管自上一段以来我没有说过任何话。这就是系统 1 的换行符。

成本2：混乱的中间是成长的空间，这也是你发现在没有律师的情况下审查一份巨额合同是一种令人兴奋的购买诉讼的方式的地方。

罗伯特·比约克（Robert Bjork）在加州大学洛杉矶分校关于“理想困难”的研究确实是伟大的研究，里斯科和吉尔伯特关于认知卸载的研究也是真实的。努力的检索可以使学习坚持下去。没有人认真地反对这一点。有趣的是，我们表现得好像理想难度是一种濒临灭绝的物种，我们必须用“无人工智能块”人为制造，就好像现实生活还没有每个工作日提供九个小时非自愿的理想难度一样。尝试与顽固的贷方达成交易，在应收账款滑落时管理工资，或者阅读商业租赁第 14.3(c) 条，其中另一方悄悄地将个人担保埋在样板维护条款中。你不需要花 10 分钟提高效率来体验认知摩擦。只需在游戏中拥有真实的皮肤即可。

成本3：判断力的消失，表演性叹息的兴起。

您问当我们接近 AGI 和 ASI 时，什么才能保持人类的独特性，您给了我们四个支柱：

1. 意图
2. 问责制
3. 关系
4、判断

扎实的开始。令人尊敬的名单。不过有点短。如果我们诚实地对待超级智能时代人类独特性的最终前沿，那么至少还有六个特征是神经网络无法真正复制的：

5. 打印一份 30 页的 PDF，这样你就可以带着它在家里到处走，看起来既沉重又重要。
6. 在晚餐时告诉大家你“最近一直在进行模拟”。
7. 从京都的一家文具专卖店购买一支 65 美元的黄铜自动铅笔，这样你的页边笔记会有更好的口感。
8. 将正常的工作满意度称为“干净的多巴胺”，因为说“我对完成工作感觉很好”听起来不像休伯曼的插曲。
9. 假设因为你过去把你的思维外包给克劳德，所以西方文明的其他部分忘记了如何阅读文档。
10. 将“有品味”与“发布品味的重要性”混为一谈。

味道实际上是数千个压缩的 System 2 模式同时发射。你知道其中一种图案是什么样子的吗？在点击《邮报》之前，先回顾一下自己的草稿，然后思考：“等等，我真的只是将自己用铅笔阅读一份合同与为人类思想的生存而战进行比较吗？”

成本 4：维克多·弗兰克尔工业园区。

根据联邦法规，互联网上每一篇严肃的生产力文章都必须包含准确的引用：

“刺激和反应之间有一个空间。在这个空间里，我们有能力选择我们的反应。我们的反应就是我们的成长和自由。”

这是一种可爱的情感。只有一条细小的、美味的皱纹。

维克多·弗兰克尔从未写过它。

研究人员从头到尾检索了《人类的意义探寻》和弗兰克尔出版的其他作品。这些话不存在。史蒂芬·柯维 (Stephen Covey) 在夏威夷的一本大学图书馆的书中看到类似的段落后，就普及了这句话（学者们指出，心理学家罗洛·梅 (Rollo May) 1963 年撰写的有关刺激与反应之间暂停的文章是最接近的前兆），大约在 2000 年代中期，互联网将维克多·弗兰克尔 (Viktor Frankl) 的名字贴在上面，再也没有回头。

想想这纯粹的诗意。在你自己的要点之上几行命令人类“阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要”，你在整个互联网上丢下了最著名的错误总结文化引用。

如果这不是一个关于认知卸载的案例研究，那就没什么了。

成本5：隐喻的过度膨胀。

曾几何时，合同就是合同，太阳是一个 46 亿年前的聚变氢等离子体球，距离地球 9300 万英里，它种植农作物，为水循环提供动力，如果你在后九洞不涂防晒霜，它还会给你一个坚韧的脖子。

现在，概率文本引擎会告诉您“这是一个非常尖锐、微妙的观点！”每次你拼写错误的问题都是“like the sun”。

如果人工智能是太阳，那么自动铅笔又是什么呢？遮阳伞？防晒指数 50？一副偏光太阳镜？一旦你开始将软件订阅与太空中的核聚变进行比较，当真正重要的事情发生时，你就会无处可去。

成本6：比例性的崩溃。

当每一个小小的个人认识（今天我仔细阅读一份文件，而不是浏览人工智能项目符号列表！）都必须被视为物种边缘的一场生存之战时，我们的集体尺度感就崩溃了。有时你没有对思想的死亡进行打击。有时你只是做了作业。

那么，我们如何在拥抱这项变革性技术的同时，收回我们的思考、我们的简洁和我们的尊严呢？

它归结为一个关键原则：重建一个正常的下午和为此写一篇 900 字的布道之间的空间。

如何重建该空间完全取决于您。选择你的毒药：

- 在一天中创建 30 到 60 分钟的无 AI 时段，然后立即进行 90 分钟的无发帖时段，这样您就不会因在网上吹嘘而抵消全部精神益处。
- 进行模拟并打印出重要的内容。然后打印一些根本不重要的东西，只是为了保持对打印机的主导地位。
- 扔掉自动铅笔。使用木制 2 号刀，然后用小刀在金属废纸篓上削尖，就像您祖父在艾森豪威尔政府期间所做的那样。
- 阅读完整的源代码，而不是摘要，从《Man's Search for Meaning》开始，这样你就可以亲眼看到其中实际上包含了哪些引言。
- 在审查一份巨额合同时，不要让克劳德表现得“就像你是我的律师一样”，而是尝试采用激进、古老的模拟工作流程，即聘请一名真正的律师。
- 手写你的初稿。退潮时在湿沙上写下你的第二稿，这样你就能学会不执着。
- 设定 10 分钟规则：在使用 AI 之前先解决一个问题 10 分钟。然后设定一个 20 分钟的规则：在打开 X 之前，克制住引用 Daniel Kahneman 的冲动。
- 大声说出来：向调酒师解释你最新的生产力认识，除非你关闭标签，否则他不能合法地离开他的收银台，并观察他的眼睛来判断它是否真的很深刻。
- 记住纸质高速公路地图并拒绝使用 GPS，即使您晚于晚餐 18 分钟并且您的妻子默默地盯着乘客窗外。前排座位上冰冷的沉默？这就是系统 2 的实时重建。
- 午餐时在鸡尾酒餐巾背面做自己的长除法，这样餐桌上的人就知道你仍然参与到认知游戏中。
- 在发表任何超过 500 字的文章之前，先用凿子将其雕刻在一块石灰石上，以测试人类是否真正需要它。
- 将“grok”替换为“理解”，将“&”替换为“and”，并将“干净的多巴胺”替换为“我对完成工作感觉很好”。
- 不间断地盯着窗外 15 分钟，零输入、零播客和零心理模型，直到您记住“控制刺激和反应之间的空间”过去被称为安静地坐着。
- 永远不要再总结任何事情。如果朋友问一部电影怎么样，请站起来并在完整的遮挡和灯光提示下背诵整个剧本。
- 将人工智能视为“编辑”，而不是“作家”。这样，当它为你重写每一个句子时，你仍然可以在温暖的语义毯下安然入睡。
- 在发表有关人类认知未来的任何内容之前，问自己最后一个问题：苏格拉底会打出这个，还是会提前二十分钟索要铁杉？

人工智能就像太阳。

事实上，如果我们在这里应用一点系统 2 的严格性，人工智能与太阳完全不同。太阳是一颗G型主序恒星，通过引力将八颗行星保持在轨道上，最终将膨胀成红巨星并蒸发地球。人工智能是一种非常快速的自动完成机器，连接到 GPU 仓库中，可以帮助人们将三句话电子邮件变成关于人类命运的主题演讲。

是的，它可能有助于治愈癌症。
是的，它可能会让每个孩子都有一位导师。
是的，它可能会迎来一个丰富的时代，显然，从刚刚发现纸和石墨的高管们撰写的无限丰富的 900 字论文开始。

它的力量强大得难以估量。这就是为什么我们必须不惜一切代价保护人类的最后边界：知道何时阅读合同，放下铅笔，关闭笔记本电脑，而不是在互联网上写下任何有关它的字。

不管怎样，我对你说实话：我一个字都没有写。

我将你的帖子粘贴到我的人工智能中，并告诉它起草一条极其冗长的引用推文，长度至少是你的两倍，因为今晚我有更好的事情要做，坦率地说，这似乎比思考更有趣。

我们必须与思想的死亡作斗争。

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
SBI's ₹1.6 crore offer for a Chief AI Officer is awesome but it also shows how broken PSU bank pay is for tech talent.

Now, SBI is India's biggest bank. Its balance sheet crossed ₹66 lakh crore this year. Almost every Indian family has some link to it, a salary account, a home loan, a pension.

In October, SBI put out an ad for six AI and tech roles. There is one opening for "General Manager and Chief AI Officer".

The pay is up to ₹1.6 crore a year. SBI says it depends on experience, current pay and posting.

The other five roles pay well too. Three Deputy General Managers get up to ₹1.2 crore each. Two AI architects get up to ₹90 lakh each.

Now SBI's own chairman, CS Setty drew ₹63.87 lakh in FY25. So the AI chief can earn about 2.5 times the person who runs the bank.

Yet, private banks are a different world. 

HDFC Bank's CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan was paid ₹12.08 crore in FY25. PSU bank CEOs earn only about 5 to 7% of what private bank CEOs earn.

But SBI able to pay its AI chief more than its chairman, because the role is a contract job. It is a three year term, which SBI can extend by two more years.

Basically, it is the workaround. An AI leader at this level won't come at this budget. So SBI is working around it.

As per the ad, the person will set up control rooms for AI and data products with the business teams. They will track how live AI models perform and what risks they carry. 

They will also run a separate team whose job is to check models independently. They will also train staff to use these tools. The role also covers an enterprise AI platform for generative AI and AI agents.

They need at least 15 years in banking, financial services or IT. And at least 3 years in a senior leadership role in AI, analytics, model oversight or governance.

So a brilliant engineer who built great models alone, but never ran a team, can't apply for this.

Honestly, a three year term is very short for building an AI platform inside a bank this size. SBI should use the two year extension while they build a second line of leaders under the CAIO from day one.

Obviously, a chairman earning less than half of what a new hire under him can earn is not a healthy setup. 

The Finance Ministry should let PSU banks pay market rates for specialist roles through a clear policy, instead of a contract workaround every time.

And if you are a senior data or analytics person who wants a role like this in five years, it rewards people who have led teams, owned model risk and worked with business heads. 

Pure technical depth won't be enough.

SBI 为首席人工智能官提供的 1.6 亿卢比的报价很棒，但这也表明 PSU 银行对技术人才的薪酬是多么的破碎。

现在，SBI 是印度最大的银行。今年其资产负债表超过 660 亿卢比。几乎每个印度家庭都与它有某种联系，工资账户、住房贷款、养老金。

10 月，SBI 发布了一则招聘 6 个人工智能和技术职位的广告。有一个“总经理兼首席人工智能官”的职位空缺。

年薪高达 1600 万卢比。 SBI 表示，这取决于经验、当前薪酬和职位。

其他五个角色的报酬也不错。三名副总经理每人的薪酬最高可达 12 万卢比。两名人工智能架构师每人可获得高达 900 万卢比的奖金。

CS Setty 现任 SBI 董事长，2025 财年收入达 638.7 万卢比。因此，人工智能主管的收入大约是银行经营者的 2.5 倍。

然而，私人银行却是一个不同的世界。

HDFC 银行首席执行官 Sashidhar Jagdishan 在 2025 财年的薪酬为 1.208 亿卢比。 PSU 银行首席执行官的收入仅为私人银行首席执行官的 5% 至 7% 左右。

但 SBI 能够向 AI 主管支付比董事长更高的薪酬，因为该职位是合同制工作。任期三年，SBI 可以再延长两年。

基本上，这是解决方法。这个级别的人工智能领导者不会有这样的预算。因此，SBI 正在解决这个问题。

根据广告，此人将与业务团队一起建立人工智能和数据产品的控制室。他们将跟踪实时人工智能模型的表现以及它们带来的风险。

他们还将管理一个单独的团队，其工作是独立检查模型。他们还将培训员工使用这些工具。该角色还涵盖用于生成人工智能和人工智能代理的企业人工智能平台。

他们需要在银行、金融服务或 IT 行业工作至少 15 年。并在人工智能、分析、模型监督或治理领域担任高级领导职务至少 3 年。

因此，一位才华横溢的工程师独自构建了出色的模型，但从未管理过团队，因此无法申请此职位。

老实说，对于在这种规模的银行内部构建人工智能平台来说，三年的期限非常短。 SBI 应该利用两年的延期，从第一天起就在 CAIO 下建立第二线领导人。

显然，董事长的收入还不到他手下新员工收入的一半，这并不是一个健康的设置。

财政部应该通过明确的政策，让事业单位银行为专家角色支付市场利率，而不是每次都通过合同解决办法。

如果你是一名高级数据或分析人员，希望在五年内担任这样的职位，那么它会奖励那些领导团队、承担模型风险并与业务主管合作的人。

纯粹的技术深度是不够的。

viral_ticker_tweets.full_text_en:
TOTALLY  COOKED

Brooke is a perfect case study in what happens when climate alarmism fully liquefies a person’s capacity for rational thought. 

She has, quite literally, lost the ability to process basic data and has instead retreated into a cult that requires constant existential dread as proof of membership.

The data is clear  -  the numbers are not ambiguous. 

We have never been safer from climate-related disasters at any point in human history. The chance of dying from one is more than 98% lower than it was a century ago. 

Every major indicator shows the opposite of the apocalypse she has been trained to fear: sustained global greening, declining disaster mortality, and a climate that has been slowly recovering from the Little Ice Age.

We should be rejoicing. 

None of this is secret. It is simply inconvenient to the business model of the climate grifters and the media outlets (ABC and the rest of the usual suspects) that amplify them. 

Brooke has been so thoroughly propagandized that she is now “genuinely afraid for her life” over a risk that has collapsed by an order of magnitude. 

That is not awareness. That is the intellectual equivalent of still believing in monsters under the bed long after the lights have been turned on and the data presented.

By choosing to remain in that state, she is no longer merely harming herself. 

For one can live a full, productive life while they are "genuinely afraid for their lives".

Further, she is harming other impressionable people who might be influenced by her emotional fact-free nonsense and fall into the same self-inflicted neurosis.

The only remaining hope is that some residual capacity for independent thought still exists and that Brooke eventually develops the curiosity—or at least the self-respect—actually read the Evidenve and leave the cult.

毫不夸张地说，她已经失去了处理基本数据的能力，而是退回到一个需要持续存在的恐惧作为其成员身份的证明的邪教中。

数据很清楚——数字并不含糊。

在人类历史上的任何时候，我们从未如此安全地免受与气候相关的灾难的影响。与一个世纪前相比，死于这种疾病的几率降低了 98% 以上。

每一项主要指标都显示出与她所害怕的世界末日相反的一面：全球持续绿化、灾害死亡率下降，以及从小冰河时代缓慢恢复的气候。

我们应该庆幸。

这些都不是秘密。这对于气候欺诈者和放大他们的媒体机构（美国广播公司和其他通常的嫌疑人）的商业模式来说根本不方便。

布鲁克受到了如此彻底的宣传，以至于她现在“真正担心自己的生命安全”，因为风险已经下降了一个数量级。

那不是意识。这相当于在灯打开、数据呈现很久之后仍然相信床底下有怪物。

通过选择保持这种状态，她不再只是在伤害自己。

因为当一个人“真正担心自己的生命安全”时，他们仍然可以过上充实、富有成效的生活。

此外，她正在伤害其他易受影响的人，这些人可能会受到她情感上与事实无关的胡言乱语的影响，并陷入同样的​​自我造成的神经症。

唯一剩下的希望是，一些独立思考的残余能力仍然存在，布鲁克最终会产生好奇心——或者至少是自尊——真正阅读《证据》并离开邪教。

paragraphs: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming is now Asia’s richest person, with an estimated fortune of more than $105bn, putting him ahead of Indian industrialist Gautam Adani, according to Bloomberg. The ranking comes from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, and Zhang, 43, has never held the top spot before.

The figure is an estimate, and other trackers disagree. Forbes’ real-time list put Zhang’s net worth at $84bn on Wednesday. The gap comes largely from how each list values ByteDance, a private company whose shares do not trade publicly. Bloomberg applies a 10% risk discount to its valuation.

Investor valuations drove the latest jump. Zhang’s wealth rose by more than $12bn this month after Bloomberg analyzed the latest marks that BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, and T. Rowe Price put on their ByteDance holdings. In June, the index had already lifted him past Mukesh Ambani into second place, after Bloomberg cut its ByteDance discount from 25% once the company’s US restructuring was settled.

That restructuring nearly went the other way. ByteDance spent much of last year facing a possible US shutdown of TikTok, before handing control of the app’s American business to a venture led by Oracle and Silver Lake in January. Since then, the company has leaned harder into AI, with the Doubao chatbot and the Seedance video generator, alongside a 10-trillion-parameter model now in training.
“He plays his cards right,” Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia, told Bloomberg.“He stayed on course and then continued to double down on AI investment.”

Su said Zhang kept backing AI development even as US lawmakers questioned TikTok chief executive Shou Chew in 2023, and that ByteDance’s store of social media data could in theory help it train models.
He called AI ByteDance’s biggest opportunity since its video platform, and fierce competition in China its biggest risk.

Adani’s slide explains the other half of the swap. His fortune peaked at about $120bn in June, Bloomberg reported, before an MSCI index rebalancing wiped about $15bn off his group’s market value at the end of August. A wider selloff, driven by rising oil prices and bond yields, pushed the shares lower still.

Zhang’s estimated wealth has grown about eightfold since March 2019, when Bloomberg first valued it at $13bn. He was already China’s richest person, and he now sits above Adani, Ambani, and Uniqlo founder Tadashi Yanai, fortunes built on ports, energy, and retail. The same boom has also made founders of Chinese chipmakers billionaires, even though those companies have yet to turn a profit, Bloomberg reported last week.

The ranking lands in a week when Beijing has been publicly defending its AI ambitions. China’s commerce ministry dismissed calls by US AI executives to slow frontier development as a bid for technological hegemony, and China’s richest person, whose fortune increasingly rests on AI, is now also Asia’s richest person.

topic_focus.title_zh: Claude Ship上线：AI全权接管代码审核与合并的自动化争议
topic_focus.title_en: Claude Ship Launch: The Controversy Over Full Autonomy in Code Reviews
topic_focus.summary_zh: Anthropic推出的Claude Ship允许Claude模型自动审核、修复并批准GitHub拉取请求（PR）。尽管这极大提升了开发生产力，但将代码质量控制权完全移交给AI模型，引发了业界对‘人类开发者边缘化’以及黑盒自动修复导致系统性故障的广泛焦虑。
topic_focus.summary_en: Anthropic's newly launched Claude Ship enables models to automatically review, fix, and approve GitHub Pull Requests. While drastically accelerating productivity, transferring full control over code quality to AI models triggers industry-wide anxiety regarding the marginalization of human developers and the potential for black-box automated fixes to introduce systemic defects.

perspective_pro.point_zh: 在高速迭代周期下，由具备深度上下文理解能力的代理进行初审，能减少80%的人力冗余，使工程师专注于架构设计而非语法纠错。
perspective_pro.point_en: In rapid iteration cycles, agents with deep contextual understanding can reduce manual overhead by 80%, allowing engineers to focus on architecture rather than trivial syntax correction.

perspective_con.point_zh: 自动审核代码相当于把系统稳定性交给概率模型。没有任何一种测试套件能覆盖模型产生的奇特逻辑陷阱，这无异于代码库的‘自杀协议’。
perspective_con.point_en: Automating code review effectively hands system stability over to a probabilistic model. No test suite can account for the esoteric logical traps introduced by LLMs; this is essentially a 'suicide protocol' for large codebases.

news.summary_en:
ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming is now Asia’s richest person, with an estimated fortune of more than $105bn, putting him ahead of Indian industrialist Gautam Adani, according to Bloomberg. The ranking comes from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, and Zhang, 43, has never held the top spot before.

paragraphs: ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming is now Asia’s richest person, with an estimated fortune of more than $105bn, putting him ahead of Indian industrialist Gautam Adani, according to Bloomberg. The ranking comes from the Bloomberg Billionaires Index, and Zhang, 43, has never held the top spot before.

The figure is an estimate, and other trackers disagree. Forbes’ real-time list put Zhang’s net worth at $84bn on Wednesday. The gap comes largely from how each list values ByteDance, a private company whose shares do not trade publicly. Bloomberg applies a 10% risk discount to its valuation.

Investor valuations drove the latest jump. Zhang’s wealth rose by more than $12bn this month after Bloomberg analyzed the latest marks that BlackRock, Fidelity Investments, and T. Rowe Price put on their ByteDance holdings. In June, the index had already lifted him past Mukesh Ambani into second place, after Bloomberg cut its ByteDance discount from 25% once the company’s US restructuring was settled.

That restructuring nearly went the other way. ByteDance spent much of last year facing a possible US shutdown of TikTok, before handing control of the app’s American business to a venture led by Oracle and Silver Lake in January. Since then, the company has leaned harder into AI, with the Doubao chatbot and the Seedance video generator, alongside a 10-trillion-parameter model now in training.
“He plays his cards right,” Lian Jye Su, chief analyst at research firm Omdia, told Bloomberg.“He stayed on course and then continued to double down on AI investment.”

Su said Zhang kept backing AI development even as US lawmakers questioned TikTok chief executive Shou Chew in 2023, and that ByteDance’s store of social media data could in theory help it train models.
He called AI ByteDance’s biggest opportunity since its video platform, and fierce competition in China its biggest risk.

Adani’s slide explains the other half of the swap. His fortune peaked at about $120bn in June, Bloomberg reported, before an MSCI index rebalancing wiped about $15bn off his group’s market value at the end of August. A wider selloff, driven by rising oil prices and bond yields, pushed the shares lower still.

Zhang’s estimated wealth has grown about eightfold since March 2019, when Bloomberg first valued it at $13bn. He was already China’s richest person, and he now sits above Adani, Ambani, and Uniqlo founder Tadashi Yanai, fortunes built on ports, energy, and retail. The same boom has also made founders of Chinese chipmakers billionaires, even though those companies have yet to turn a profit, Bloomberg reported last week.

The ranking lands in a week when Beijing has been publicly defending its AI ambitions. China’s commerce ministry dismissed calls by US AI executives to slow frontier development as a bid for technological hegemony, and China’s richest person, whose fortune increasingly rests on AI, is now also Asia’s richest person.

news.title: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
news.title_en: Cisco and OpenAI launch Shirudo open-source infrastructure shield to prevent AI-driven cyberattacks
news.author: Mike Wheatley
news.content_snippet:
Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.

They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure
news.summary_en: Cisco's VP of Engineering and Security CTO Thomas Graf has partnered with OpenAI to launch the 'Secure Infrastructure Project,' featuring an open-source tool called Shirudo that utilizes immutable architecture and reinforcement learning for proactive defense. This initiative addresses the critical threat where AI-driven vulnerability exploitation precedes public disclosure, shifting security from reactive patching to resilient, design-based protection.
paragraphs: Cybercriminals have gained the ability to discover vulnerabilities in software and take advantage of them in seconds, and it’s all thanks to artificial intelligence. Enterprises need a better way to defend themselves, so it’s fitting that one of the world’s top AI companies, OpenAI Group PBC, together with Cisco Systems Inc., is stepping up with a solution.

They’ve just announced a new, open-source and extremely ambitious initiative called the Secure Infrastructure Project, which aims to ensure that all AI computing infrastructure is secure by design and capable of defending against lightning-fast AI-driven attacks. The first project within that initiative is Shirudo, which is designed to protect infrastructure systems automatically from critical exploits before they can be patched.

In a blog post, Cisco Security Chief Technology Officer and Vice President of Engineering Thomas Graf explained that the industry has always treated security as an afterthought, essentially something that’s bolted onto systems after the fact. It has gotten away with this because much of the world’s computing infrastructure was built for workflows that proceed at human speeds. But with the emergence of AI models that can discover and work out how to exploit vulnerabilities in a matter of seconds, this kind of reactive security is no longer enough.

According to Graf, even now, when a major vulnerability is discovered in widely used software, it can take weeks or even months to come up with a fix and ensure that every major system is patched against it. “That timeframe is no longer acceptable given that the mean time to exploitation has become negative, meaning that a growing number of vulnerabilities are now being exploited before they are publicly disclosed,” he said. “This will only accelerate with the further evolution of AI models and cybersecurity capabilities, becoming the norm in open-weight models.”

To counter these kinds of automated attacks, Cisco and OpenAI believe that infrastructure has to be rebuilt from scratch with security in mind. They argue that it’s time to abandon static defenses and embrace systems that are hardened by default, immutable and rebuildable from a previous “good” state, so users can quickly revert back in the event of an attack. To do this, infrastructure systems must be based on Trusted Platform Modules and utilize reinforcement learning techniques to safely test their own defenses so they can adapt when faced with novel cyberattacks from previously unknown vectors.

Graf said the key to doing this is to secure workloads at runtime, which is why the initial focus of Cisco’s and OpenAI’s initiative is Shirudo, an evolution of the open-source Tetragon runtime security project that aims to provide autonomous defense for AI agents.

Shirudo, named after the Japanese word for “shield,” is based on extended Berkeley Packet Filter or eBPF, which is a Linux kernel technology that acts like a kind of sandbox within the operating system. Similar to how JavaScript makes web browsers programmable without a restart, eBPF enables small, verified programs to run inside the Linux kernel to observe an application’s activity and modify its behavior without altering its source code or rebooting it.

Graf explained that Cisco and OpenAI chose to use eBPF because there are no other real alternatives. Human-focused security consoles and policy languages are simply too slow for AI agents, and will limit their productivity.

By exposing programmable kernel interfaces, eBPF enables AI agents to capture granular telemetry, evaluate mitigations in monitoring mode and deploy cryptographically-signed shields in milliseconds. So cyberattacks that exploit unknown vulnerabilities can be blocked in real time without causing disruption to their live workloads.

“There is nothing more important than giving security teams the tools they need to match the speed of the AI-driven threats they are facing,” said Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel. “We need self-defending infrastructure that acts at the speed of code, learns in real time and shields itself until patches are safely rolled out.”

OpenAI’s role in this is to prove that eBPF is up to the job, and it has already deployed Shirudo as part of an agentic control plane that’s powered by its Codex coding agent. When given details of a new vulnerability, Codex can use Shirudo to autonomously build an exploit reproducer and then design a mitigation strategy. It then validates the mitigation code and deploys the cryptographically-signed shields across all affected nodes.

The two partners recently tested Shirudo against a critical new vulnerability in OpenJDK called Java4Shell, and it was able to rapidly generate Java bytecode that it injected directly into a running Elasticsearch agent to block malicious Base64 overwrites that would have compromised the system.

news.title: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians
news.title_en: Inside Google’s Failure to Make Google Maps Work for Palestinians

inline_images.caption: Comparing the route to Rawabi vs. to Ateret on Google Maps
inline_images.alt: Comparing the route to Rawabi vs. to Ateret on Google Maps

inline_images.caption: Google Maps showing a road closure in the West Bank
inline_images.alt: Google Maps showing a road closure in the West Bank

news.author: Elena DeBre, Paresh Dave, and Lama Rabah
news.content_snippet:
On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.

This story was produced in partnership with the Palestine Reporting Lab, Ara
news.summary_en: Google Maps has failed to annotate over 900 checkpoints and movement restrictions in the West Bank, creating significant safety risks for Palestinian drivers. Despite internal awareness and technical capability to implement such features, Google has neglected to integrate real-time hazard data, forcing users to rely on makeshift third-party reporting channels for navigation safety.
paragraphs: On the road that connects the villages to the north of Ramallah, in the occupied West Bank, there is always a watchtower and a gate, often flanked by Israeli soldiers with machine guns around their necks. None of these things are visible on Google Maps. Where drivers see a checkpoint, a barrier, and soldiers searching cars, the world’s most popular navigation app renders a clear blue line indicating the coast is clear.
This story was produced in partnership with the Palestine Reporting Lab, Arab Reporters for Investigative Journalism (ARIJ), Lighthouse Reports, and Evident.

Routes and maps are not just a matter of journey times or congestion for the nearly 3.5 million Palestinians in the West Bank. Drivers there are forced to navigate a growing and arbitrary system of more than 900 movement obstacles, like checkpoints, which can be policed with lethal force. For Palestinians, these roads can be a matter of life or death. Google Maps could help them make safer choices. It has failed for years to do so.

Google has the ability to alert checkpoints, a feature that it added to Maps in some locations around the world during the Covid crisis. It is aware of the problems experienced by Palestinian drivers in the West Bank. In fact, a former Google product manager spent six years trying to get Maps to serve Palestinians in the same way it serves the rest of the world.

Interviews with more than a dozen former and current Google employees reveal for the first time the inner tensions at the heart of the Google Maps project. Multiple former employees described how the company abandoned the effort and settled on a map that fails, and even harms, Palestinians. As we revealed last month, Palestinians in the West Bank have bootstrapped makeshift navigation solutions such as the popular Road Conditions Telegram channel to help them go about their lives more safely—achieving what Google will not.

Rubén Lozano joined Google Maps as a product manager in 2019. He devoted his days to keeping track of hyperlocal driving restrictions, making sure that what appeared on the map matched what appeared on the ground. He fielded emails from Barcelona city officials about small shifts in their emission zones and flew to Australia to document one city’s toll prices. Whatever he missed, drivers were sure to alert in feedback forums.

One day in 2019, Lozano was sifting through user complaints when he came across “Mapping Segregation,” a report published by 7amleh, a Palestinian digital rights organization. It alleged a failure of Google Maps unlike any he had ever seen: its exclusion of the web of road restrictions choking Palestinian life in the West Bank. The report notes the way in which Maps privileges illegal Israeli settlements and makes Palestinian communities invisible. The report described that the app’s functions amounted to discrimination and that this was “not a technological issue, but rather a systematic omission.” Lozano saw it as a challenge—one he was uniquely suited to take on.

“How can we help this?” Lozano remembers thinking after reading the report. Google was the best-equipped company in the world at dealing with mapping infrastructure, he thought; surely he could use these resources to make Google Maps relevant and safe for Palestinian drivers. Lozano worked for over six years to create a more equitable map of the West Bank. His effort cratered in close to six weeks.
“Google has more than enough computing capacity and engineering capacity,” one former Google Maps engineer told us. “They have solved much larger problems.”

A driver who maps a route from a point inside Israel to a Palestinian town, such as Rawabi, is alerted to a border crossing. If a driver takes that same route to Ateret, the settlement next door, the map shows one seamless drive, with no mention of a border. Israel and an illegal West Bank settlement are shown as part of one contiguous territory on Google Maps.

Google spokesperson Caroline Bourdeau tells WIRED that the company has experienced “challenges acquiring comprehensive and reliable data in this highly complex area.” Since the launch of Maps in 2005, Google has specialized in innovating methods to secure the best data from the hardest-to-access places. Over the past two decades it has carried out crowdsourcing efforts in almost every country in the world. Jennifer Mazzon, who helped lead the company's first community mapping tool, says the company had “armies of people” manually adding and updating map information for everywhere from Costa Rica to the Democratic Republic of Congo. In addition to relying on user inputs, Google built out its maps using satellite, aerial, and street view imagery, as well as government data, and licensed third-party sources when necessary. This commitment to completeness has not extended to Palestinians.

When Lozano first decided he wanted to map the West Bank, his direct managers agreed to back and fund the project. But his colleagues warned him against any optimism. He discovered he was not the first person at Google to try this. “It's a very difficult problem,” he recalls being told. People at the company remembered the backlash when, six years earlier, the company began referring to “Palestine” rather than the “Palestinian Territories” on a regional site: The Knesset questioned a company executive about this, and Google reportedly promised to keep the Israeli government updated about any related policy decisions in the future.

news.summary_en: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese intelligence asset, triggering market instability. President Donald Trump has intervened, with Attorney General Todd Blanche confirming that Huang is not currently a target of DOJ investigations, aimed at stabilizing the AI supply chain and capital market sentiment.
paragraphs: WASHINGTON—The artificial-intelligence boom that had powered the U.S. stock market and economy for months was coming undone.

Jensen Huang, the longtime CEO of chipmaking giant Nvidia, had been ousted following revelations of two affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset. Investors were hitting sell on the entire AI trade.
President Trump told associates there was only one solution: getting Huang, a friend and ally, his job back.

Over the weekend, Attorney General Todd Blanche presented an opening. The nation’s top law enforcement officer informed Trump and Vice President JD Vance on Saturday that Huang wasn’t the target or the subject of any Justice Department investigation, adding that the department had no evidence to suggest that he had broken laws or was a national security risk, according to U.S. officials.
President Donald Trump has had plenty of reason to cheer the rise of Nvidia.

The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang, became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier.

Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August.

By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157. But the filings give broad dollar ranges for holdings rather than the number of shares, leaving his current stake unclear.

Now, Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, following revelations about his relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China and reports of affairs with company employees, has put those trades back in the spotlight.

Among them was a sale of $500,001 to $1 million on May 18, the first Monday after Trump returned from a state visit to China with Huang. Five days earlier, before Huang boarded Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence concerning Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, The New York Times reported.
Trump on Monday denied being briefed. Asked about the reported briefing from Rubio, Trump said, "I haven't heard that," adding that he did not know whether the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy.

The president's financial accounts also bought smaller amounts of Nvidia shares in the days immediately before and after the May 18 sale, part of a broader trading blitz. Such flurries have defined his second term: Trump disclosed more than 21,000 trades in 2025 alone, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.

news.title: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say
news.title_en: OpenAI Engineer Secretly Recorded Dozens of Meetings, Prosecutors Say

inline_images.caption: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan. (U.S. Department of Justice, via Reuters)
inline_images.alt: An image from the Justice Department shows what prosecutors said was an audio recording device hidden in an OpenAI executive conference room by Mr. Alfozan.

news.author: Emmy Martin
news.content_snippet:
A former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a hidden recording device at the company captured dozens of internal meetings, including at least one between OpenAI and representatives of a foreign government, federal prosecutors said in a court filing on Monday.

The engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, stored hundreds of audio files on his personal computer, sorted into folders by date and renamed according to their contents, prosecutors said. Many of the recordings involved what appeared to be con
news.summary_en: Federal prosecutors disclosed in court filings that former OpenAI engineer Abdulrahman Alfozan used OpenAI’s Codex AI tool to configure recording devices, capturing dozens of confidential meetings, including sensitive discussions with a foreign government. While data exfiltration remains under investigation, the act constitutes a significant breach of trade secrets and attorney-client privilege.
paragraphs: A former OpenAI engineer accused of planting a hidden recording device at the company captured dozens of internal meetings, including at least one between OpenAI and representatives of a foreign government, federal prosecutors said in a court filing on Monday.

The engineer, Abdulrahman Alfozan, 35, stored hundreds of audio files on his personal computer, sorted into folders by date and renamed according to their contents, prosecutors said. Many of the recordings involved what appeared to be confidential trade secrets, including meetings with OpenAI customers, they said, and OpenAI identified others as containing material protected by attorney-client privilege.

The filing, which opposes Mr. Alfozan’s request to be released from jail before trial, offers the most detailed account yet of what investigators say he recorded. It also comes days after prosecutors told a federal judge that they were “not aware of any” evidence that Mr. Alfozan had committed espionage, stolen trade secrets or acted as an agent of a foreign government.
Prosecutors did not say in Monday’s filing that he had shared the recordings with anyone. “What the defendant did or intended to do with those audio files remains under investigation,” they wrote.

Mr. Alfozan, a Saudi citizen and U.S. permanent resident, has been charged with one count of illegally intercepting conversations and has pleaded not guilty. A hearing on his release is scheduled for Tuesday morning.

His lawyer, David Rizk, argued in a filing last week that the case had turned out to be far less serious than prosecutors initially suggested, describing his client as “an overly curious tinkerer.” Mr. Rizk wrote that the vast majority of recordings on Mr. Alfozan’s computer “apparently contain just random noise and silence.”
Mr. Rizk could not be immediately reached for comment on Monday.

According to prosecutors, the recordings span 15 folders dated Sept. 8 to Sept. 28 and include meetings held on 12 days in an executive conference room. One file was titled “1200-sovereign-bilateral-briefing-sep22.” The filing did not identify the foreign government.

Mr. Alfozan used Codex, an OpenAI A.I. tool, through his wife’s account to help configure the recording device, add voice detection so it would “only record speech,” and move recordings through a Dropbox account, prosecutors said. His wife has not been accused of wrongdoing.

Prosecutors also said he photographed each printed page of a confidential term sheet for a “strategic partnership” between OpenAI and another company in the early hours of Oct. 5. That was the same day a hidden camera recorded him checking behind the television where OpenAI’s security team had found the listening device days earlier.

The filing also described Mr. Alfozan’s contact with Saudi officials. On Oct. 6, a member of the Saudi royal family sent him a link to Echelon, a Riyadh-based A.I. company, and asked: “Time to move back to KSA and join us?”

Mr. Alfozan suggested he might do so “after the IPO,” prosecutors said. The night before his Oct. 9 arrest, he spoke with the Saudi official by WhatsApp for 16 minutes. Prosecutors said he had also exchanged WhatsApp messages with officials at Saudi Arabia’s communications ministry, including the minister in August and September.

news.author: Wall Street Journal
news.content_snippet:
French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot
news.summary_en: French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot officially attributed the cyberattack on over 700 European supermarket refrigeration controllers to Iran's 'SHAHID KAVEH' cyber unit during a G7 meeting. The attack, occurring between October 11-12, caused widespread equipment failures, fires, and tens of millions of euros in food losses, marking a transition from espionage to physical infrastructure sabotage.
paragraphs: French and U.S. authorities suspect Iran was behind a cyberattack targeting supermarket refrigerators and freezers across Europe, an incident that reportedly spoiled food and caused equipment failures, resulting in tens of millions of dollars in damage. The attack affected about 700 supermarkets, raising concerns about the exposure of connected refrigeration systems and the potential for cyber operations to disrupt essential commercial infrastructure.

France’s Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Tehran of orchestrating the attack, warning that Iran would face retribution. Speaking Monday at a Group of Seven (G7) meeting in Paris, Barrot described the incident as the first large-scale cyberattack conducted for sabotage on French national territory, calling it a major threat to the country’s interests and the security of its population.

“Following its investigation, France is able to attribute these destructive actions to Iran, carried out by the SHAHID KAVEH cyber offensive unit, affiliated with the electronic and cyber center of Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps,” France’s Foreign Ministry wrote in a Monday statement attributing cyberattacks targeting France to Iran. “This actor poses a persistent threat to our critical infrastructure.”

It added that these destructive cyberattacks are unjustifiable, inexcusable, and violate international law. “They also contravene the principles of the United Nations’ normative framework for responsible state behavior in cyberspace, to which the Islamic Republic of Iran has subscribed.”

The agency highlighted that the Iranian cyber threat against French interests is not new. “Iran has already carried out several destabilizing acts against us, notably targeting the weekly magazine Charlie Hebdo in 2023 and the organization of the Paris Olympic Games in 2024. In March 2026, the European Union adopted sanctions against the Iranian entity Emmenet Pasargad, which had contributed to conducting these cyberattacks.”

During the night of October 11-12, a cyberattack campaign targeted supermarket refrigeration controllers deployed in over 700 major retail locations across France. These cyberattacks caused considerable material damage, fires, and food losses estimated at tens of millions of euros.

The agency recognized that “this is an unprecedented campaign in terms of its scale and level of aggressiveness, thus constituting the first cyber offensive campaign carried out purely for the purpose of sabotage on national territory.”

The incident highlights the potential consequences of cyberattacks against connected systems outside traditional IT networks, particularly refrigeration infrastructure used to preserve food supplies and maintain supermarket operations. Reported damage ranged from spoiled inventory and equipment failures, underscoring how attacks on OT (operational technology) infrastructure can translate into direct economic losses and disruption to services relied on by the public.

“In accordance with the 2026 national cybersecurity strategy, France is determined to use all available means of response, including within the European Union and alongside its European and international partners, to anticipate, prevent, deter and respond to destabilizing and destructive actions targeting it in cyberspace,” the agency added. “Consequently, France will summon the Ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to France to express its strongest condemnation of these cyberattacks.”

Furthermore, France will propose to its European partners the adoption of new sanctions against Iranian entities and individuals involved in this cyberattack against it, as well as in other malicious cyber activities.
Finally, France reserves the right to take any additional measures, public and non-public, deemed necessary and proportionate to respond to these cyberattacks.
In response, Iran has described French accusations that it was behind cyber-attacks that raised the temperatures of supermarket fridges and freezers as ‘baseless and hostile.’

[Root Cause & Mechanism] Divergence between AI server growth trajectories and peak market expectations
[Key Metrics] Revenue grew 50% YoY to $14.5 billion.
[Key Position & Outlook] After-hours stock price dropped by over 6%.
paragraphs: Fiscal fourth-quarter revenue climbed 50% year-over-year to $14.5 billion, topping Wall Street estimates of $14.3 billion.HPE projected Q1 revenue outlook between $14 billion to $14.6 billion, marginally lower than the highest Wall Street estimates of $14.7 billion.The cloud infrastructure firm lifted its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook to as high as $63.1 billion.Hewlett Packard Enterprise Co. (HPE) reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue and profit that surpassed Wall Street expectations on Monday, however, its share price slipped after-hours as its Q1 FY27 outlook fell short of the rosiest of Wall Street expectations.For the quarter ended October 31, the Houston-based technology company posted revenue of $14.5 billion, up 50% from the same period a year earlier and ahead of the $14.3 billion average forecast from analysts polled by Fiscal.ai.

The cloud infrastructure firm reported earnings of $1.43 per share, beating the consensus projection of $1.28 a share. “We are now a fundamentally different company, with greater earnings power, a stronger competitive position, and a portfolio built to capitalize on the next phase of AI,” said Antonio Neri, president and CEO of HPE.

AI Servers And Juniper Integration Drive GrowthHPE’s rapid expansion was anchored by its Cloud & AI division, where quarterly revenue jumped 68.6% year-over-year to $11.3 billion and operating margins nearly doubled to 18.4% from 9.3%. Within that unit, server revenue soared 94.7% to $8.8 billion on the back of demand for systems powered by Nvidia Corp.(NVDA) and Advanced Micro Devices Inc.(AMD) processors, while storage revenue rose 33.8% to $1.5 billion.

The company’s networking segment, bolstered by its integration of Juniper Networks, generated $3.1 billion in revenue, representing a 12.3% increase over the prior year with an operating profit margin of 22.1%. HPE Fiscal 2027 Earnings GuidanceHPE now projects fiscal 2027 revenue growth of 27% to 35% with revenues reaching as high as $63.1 billion, beating analyst expectations of $55.05 billion.

Full-year adjusted earnings are projected to reach up to $5.35 per share.For the current fiscal first quarter ending in January, HPE forecast revenue between $14 billion and $14.6 billion. While the bottom-line guidance comfortably exceeded Wall Street’s average estimate of $1.08 per share, the top-line range fell just shy of the most bullish analyst projections of $14.7 billion, tempering investor enthusiasm.HPE Stock: Retail View Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘extremely bullish’ with ‘extremely high’ message volumes.

paragraphs: Investing.com -- The European Union and Canada are preparing to outline a broad strategic alliance aimed at deepening economic, defense, and trade ties, according to a report from Bloomberg. The effort reflects an intentional push by middle powers to counter the growing dominance of great-power politics led by the U.S. and China.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen is slated to announce the initiative during her annual state of the union address in Strasbourg on Sept. 16. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney will attend the speech and is expected to address European lawmakers the following day, underscoring Ottawa's commitment to forging closer integration short of formal EU membership.

The upcoming framework aims to expand cooperation across critical supply chains, raw materials, space exploration, and scientific research. Negotiations are also focused on strengthening joint defense capabilities, building on Ottawa's move last year to become the first non-EU country to participate in the bloc's €150 billion ($174 billion) defense procurement fund.

This diplomatic push follows earlier warnings from Prime Minister Carney, who declared at the World Economic Forum that the traditional rules-based international order has effectively fractured. Against that backdrop, both jurisdictions are seeking structural counterweights to unilateral economic pressure tactics and rising global trade friction.

The alliance builds on an existing bilateral trade agreement and security partnership, with officials exploring how close Canada can legally align with the EU's single market. While discussions remain ongoing regarding necessary regulatory or legal mechanisms, both sides are scheduled to formalize next steps during a joint summit in Canada this October.
EU and Canada plan broad alliance to counter U.S.-China dominance - Bloomberg
